errorMessage.description: a message that will be displayed inside a toast in case of error

fanOutPath.description: name of an ARRAY field in the submitted values: the action fans out into ONE ordered write per element (for each write, that field is replaced by the single element before payload/payloadToOverride interpolation). The whole set is gated behind ONE aggregated blast-radius confirm and dispatched sequentially with stop-on-first-error and per-item results (W0-4 applySet semantics); onEventNavigateTo is not supported on a fan-out action

ops.description: ordered list of DISTINCT writes applied as ONE gated set (e.g. one Form submit creating a Role AND its RoleBinding): each op resolves its OWN resourceRefId (verb + path + payload base) and builds its OWN payload/payloadToOverride against the SAME submitted values. The whole set is gated behind ONE aggregated blast-radius confirm and dispatched sequentially with stop-on-first-error and per-item results (W0-4 applySet semantics). Mutually exclusive with fanOutPath; onEventNavigateTo is not supported on a multi-op action. The action's own top-level payload/payloadToOverride are IGNORED when ops is present and its top-level resourceRefId is ignored for dispatch (it must still name a valid resource ref — point it at the first op's)

resourceRefId.description: the identifier of the resource ref this op targets: its verb (must be mutating), path and payload base

payload.description: static payload sent with this op's request

payloadToOverride.description: list of this op's payload fields to override dynamically (values interpolate against the same submitted values as every other op)

name.description: name of the field to override

value.description: value to use for overriding the field

successMessage.description: a message that will be displayed inside a toast in case of success

onSuccessNavigateTo.description: url to navigate to after successful execution

onEventNavigateTo.description: conditional navigation triggered by a specific event

eventReason.description: identifier of the awaited event reason

url.description: url to navigate to when the event is received

timeout.description: the timeout in seconds to wait for the event

reloadRoutes.description: Re-fetch the route table before navigating. Set it when the action creates its own destination — publishing a new page, for example — so the route exists by the time the navigation happens.

loadingMessage.description: message to display while waiting for the event

headers.description: array of headers as strings, format 'key: value'

items.description: key and value as a single, example: 'x-custom-header: value'

payload.description: static payload sent with the request

payloadToOverride.description: list of payload fields to override dynamically

value.description: value to use for overriding the field

customWidth.description: the custom width of the value, which should be used by setting the 'custom' value inside the 'size' property

autocomplete.description: Configuration for the Autocomplete form fields. The field options could be configured using enum values coming from the schema or via an API call made using a RESTAction which sould be defined below. The RESTActions shuold contain a `status` field, which is an array of object with the `{ label, value }` format.

extra.description: parameter to be added to the RESTAction call

key.description: the key of the additional parameter

name.description: the name of the autocomplete field

resourceRefId.description: the identifier of the RESTAction that should be called to retrieve autocomplete data

closed.description: true: only a listed value is accepted (a select); false: the list suggests and typed text is kept. Default false (the previous frontend rendered autocomplete fields as an autocomplete)

minChars.description: with `extra`: the typed text is sent once it has this many characters. Default 2

fallback.description: `manual`: a closed field whose options cannot be loaded (the RESTAction fails, or answers an empty list) takes a typed value instead of blocking the form

buttonConfig.description: custom labels and icons for form buttons

block.description: when true, the primary button spans the whole action bar (antd Button `block`), with any other button stacked above it

size.description: antd Button `size` of the primary button

navigateTo.description: when set, the secondary button is a Cancel that navigates to this route (SPA) instead of resetting the form

hidden.description: when true, the secondary button (Reset, or the Cancel of `navigateTo`) is not shown

draft.description: draft button configuration — only rendered when widgetData.draftActionId is also set; clicking it persists the current (un-validated) field values via that action

review.description: Configure-step button label when reviewBeforeSubmit is set (the button that opens the in-place Review; default 'Review →')

label.description: text label for the Review button

reviewBack.description: Review-step back button label when reviewBeforeSubmit is set (returns to editing; default '← Back to edit')

label.description: text label for the back-to-edit button

checkboxes.description: boolean fields drawn as a Checkbox whose text is the field's label (its schema `title`, else its key), where a boolean is otherwise a Switch. The label is plain text; one phrase of it can be a link. A REQUIRED checkbox must be ticked to submit

name.description: the dotted path of a boolean field; an entry naming any other field is ignored

link.description: one link in the label: the first occurrence of `text` in the label becomes a link to `href`, opened in a new tab (when `text` is not in the label, the link follows it)

text.description: the phrase of the label that is the link

href.description: an http(s) or mailto URL, or a path on the portal (`/…`), with no whitespace or control characters; any other is not drawn as a link

requiredMessage.description: the message under a required checkbox left unticked

dependencies.description: Configuration for the form fields who are dependent from other form fields. The field options are set via an API call made using a RESTAction which sould be defined below. The RESTActions shuold contain a `status` field, which is an array of object with the `{ label, value }` format.

dependsOn.description: the field on which this field depends on

name.description: the name of the field on which this field depends on

extra.description: parameter to be added to the RESTAction call

key.description: the key of the additional parameter

name.description: the name of the autocomplete field

resourceRefId.description: the identifier of the RESTAction that should be called to retrieve dependency data

closed.description: true: only a listed value is accepted (a select); false: the list suggests and typed text is kept. Default true (the previous frontend rendered dependent fields as a select)

fallback.description: `manual`: a closed field whose options cannot be loaded (the RESTAction fails, or answers an empty list) takes a typed value instead of blocking the form

displayingDependencies.description: Configuration for the form fields whose displaying is dependent from other form fields.

dependsOn.description: the field on which this field depends on

name.description: the name of the field on which this field depends on

conditionType.description: `notEmpty` (default) indicates that the current field is displayed if the dependency field has a non-empty value. `value` indicates that the current field is displayed only when the dependency field matches a specific value.

optionValue.description: Value if type = option: includes a single value or a { label, value } object

value.description: Value of the option. A number or a boolean is compared with type integer or boolean.

draftActionId.description: optional id of an action fired by a 'Save draft' button that captures the CURRENT field values WITHOUT running form validation (so an incomplete form can be persisted). Pair with buttonConfig.draft to show the button.

fieldChecks.description: fields checked against a same-origin endpoint as they are typed: after typing pauses and on blur, the field's value (with `bodyExtras`) is POSTed as JSON and the answer becomes the field's validation status and message. A newer value aborts the check in flight; an answer for an old value is never applied. An empty value, or one failing the field's own rules, is not checked. While a check runs the field shows antd's validating spinner, and a submit waits for that answer

name.description: the dotted path of the field to check (a text-like field: not a boolean, object or list)

path.description: the same-origin path to POST JSON to. Sent through the page transport's allow-listed post: the path must be under one of the installation's PUBLIC_POST_PATHS, and no credential is ever sent (public page or signed in). Any other path is refused unsent

bodyKey.description: the body key the value is sent under; the last segment of `name` when absent

bodyExtras.description: body key → the name of one of the page's fragment extras (the keys its root declares in `krateo.io/fragment-keys`), e.g. `{ submission: s, token: t }`: those values are sent in the request BODY, never in a URL, and never enter the form. A key the page was not opened with is left out

debounceMs.description: how long typing must pause before the check is sent, in milliseconds; 500 when absent. Blur sends it at once

timeoutMs.description: the client timeout in milliseconds; 10000 when absent. A timeout is `otherwise`. Leave room for an endpoint that holds its answer

answers.description: what each answer means for the field, tried in order (first match wins)

when.description: which answers this entry is for. Every condition given must hold; one left out matches anything. Entries are tried in order and the first match wins. An entry with no `when` matches every answer (entries after it are never reached). A request that got no answer (a network error, the client timeout) matches no entry: it is `otherwise`

bodyField.description: a dotted path into the JSON response body, e.g. `status`; the entry matches only when that field is a string listed in `equals`

equals.description: the values `bodyField` may hold for this entry to match

validateStatus.description: the field's validation status for this answer (`warning` when absent). `error` blocks submitting, `warning` does not; `success` shows `message` as the field's help

message.description: the message under the field; may name `{value}` (the checked value), `{body.<dotted>}` and `{retryAfter}`

retryAfterMessage.description: the message instead of `message` when the answer carries a Retry-After of a positive number of seconds; `{retryAfter}` is that wait ("30 seconds", or whole minutes above 60: "2 minutes"), stated once, with no countdown

ruleFrom.description: a dotted path into the response body naming a rule, e.g. `rule`; its `ruleMessages` entry replaces `message`

result.description: an antd Result that REPLACES the form (and its buttons). Its strings may name `{body.<dotted>}` (a value from the response, e.g. `{body.username}`), `{value}` (a checked field's value) and `{retryAfter}`; they are plain text, never markup

icon.description: an icon name, as buttonConfig takes them (e.g. `fa-envelope`), in place of the status icon

kind.description: `button`: an antd primary Button; `link`: a plain link, after `text`

label.description: the button's or the link's text

href.description: an http(s) or mailto URL, or a path on the portal (`/…`, opened inside the app), with no whitespace or control characters; any other drops this action

text.description: plain text before a `link`, e.g. `Already have an account?`

fieldHelp.description: help text shown UNDER a field's input (antd Form.Item `extra`), where it stays in view while a validation message shows above it. Plain text

name.description: the dotted path of a field (not an object or a list)

fieldInputs.description: a field's input: its placeholder, its HTML input type and its autocomplete token. `placeholder` applies to a text Input, a TextArea and a Select (in place of "Select…"); `type` and `autoComplete` to a text Input (`autoComplete` to a TextArea too). An entry naming a group, a list, a boolean, a number or a secret field is ignored

autoComplete.description: the input's `autocomplete` attribute: one autofill field name of the HTML standard (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#autofill), or `on` / `off`. Credential and payment tokens are not offered: a secret field has its own

name.description: the dotted path of a field

placeholder.description: the text the empty control shows

type.description: the text Input's HTML type: the keyboard a phone shows and what the browser offers to fill. The form's own rules still validate the value: with a `type`, the form turns off the browser's constraint validation (`novalidate`), so its errors show under the field like every other

hasFeedback.description: which fields of a schema form show antd's validation feedback icons. Absent: required fields. `rules`: every field with a validation rule, required or optional (an optional field shows the success icon only once it holds a value). `none`: no field, a `fieldChecks` field included

initialValues.description: optional object with initial values for form fields. Keys should match form field names (supports nested objects). These values override schema defaults.

items.description: resourceRefIds of form-control widgets (Input, Select, Switch, …) to compose inside the Form. Composable mode — an alternative to the schema/stringSchema generator.

resourceRefId.description: the identifier of the form-control widget to render

notice.description: a message shown above the fields of a schema form (e.g. the blueprint formdef's note that the form was built from the CRD)

noticeVariant.description: how `notice` is drawn: `alert` (absent), an info Alert; `text`, a line of secondary text. Either goes with the form when a Result replaces it

objectFields.description: configuration for object fields in the form

path.description: the path of the object field

displayField.description: the field to display in the objects list

propertiesToHide.description: top-level schema property names to omit from the schema-driven form

requiredMark.description: antd Form requiredMark. `optional`: required fields carry no mark and every other field reads "(optional)"; in a schema form the optional fields then render in place, in schema order, instead of in the "Advanced" collapse. Absent: required fields are marked with an asterisk. `hidden`: no field carries a mark, required or not (antd `requiredMark={false}`)

reviewBeforeSubmit.description: when true (inline render only), the primary button validates and reveals an in-place read-only Review of the entered values before the real submit — the form stays mounted so 'Back to edit' preserves every value. Pair with buttonConfig.review / buttonConfig.reviewBack for custom labels.

schema.description: JSON schema (e.g. a blueprint CRD's openAPIV3Schema spec) rendered as form fields — the schema-driven alternative to `items`. Usually populated server-side via a widgetDataTemplate jq expression that extracts the spec schema. Note: a schema sourced from a CRD's openAPIV3Schema has its `properties` map serialized alphabetically (order lost); use `stringSchema` to preserve the source values.schema.json authoring order.

stringSchema.description: Same JSON schema as `schema`, but as a raw JSON STRING. Preferred over `schema` when present: the client JSON.parses it, preserving key insertion order, so fields render in the source values.schema.json order rather than the alphabetized order a CRD-sourced object schema yields. Typically populated server-side from the blueprint's per-version jsonschema ConfigMap (which keeps authoring order). Falls back to `schema` when absent or not valid JSON.

submitActionId.description: the id of the action to be called when the form is submitted. A Form submits EITHER through `actions` + `submitActionId` OR through `submitPost`; with neither or both it renders an error

submitActionSelector.description: optional field-conditional submit routing: when present, the submit action is chosen at submit time from the value of the named field. Routes one form to different create targets (e.g. a 'target cluster' select where 'local' posts the blueprint instance and a remote spoke posts a RemoteInstall). Falls back to `default` (or `submitActionId`) when the field value has no mapping.

field.description: form field whose current value selects the submit action

default.description: action id used when the field value is not present in `map`

submitDisabledWhenPristine.description: when true, the primary (submit) button stays disabled until at least one field differs from its initial value (initialValues overlaid on schema defaults). name.description: Name of the RESTAction resource to call.

apiRef.description: Binds this widget to a RESTAction whose response feeds the widgetDataTemplate and resourcesRefsTemplate expressions. Omit it for a widget whose data is entirely static.

forPath.description: Dot-path inside widgetData whose value this expression replaces, for example `items[0].title`.

expression.description: A jq expression evaluated server-side against the apiRef response. Its result replaces the value at forPath.

widgetDataTemplate.description: Per-field overrides evaluated against the apiRef response, so one authored widget can render live cluster data. Each entry replaces one value inside widgetData.

allowed.description: Set server-side: whether the caller may perform this verb. False entries are stripped before the widget renders and are never authored by hand.

apiVersion.description: Group and version of the referenced resource, for example `widgets.templates.krateo.io/v1beta1`.

id.description: The author-chosen handle this widget uses to reference the resource, matching a resourceRefId in widgetData.

payload.description: Body sent with a mutating verb. Ignored for a GET.

verb.description: HTTP verb used to resolve the reference. GET for a read; a mutating verb makes this a write the widget can dispatch.

offset.description: Number of items to skip before the returned page.

perPage.description: Maximum items in the returned page.

continue.description: Opaque continuation token from a previous response, used to fetch the next page.

slice.description: Server-side paging for this reference: the widget receives one page rather than the whole list.

items.description: One referenced resource. The widget addresses it by its `id`, never by name.

resourcesRefs.description: The resources this widget references by id. Each entry is resolved server-side and its endpoint handed to the widget; entries the caller may not read are removed before the widget renders, so a denied reference reads as absence rather than as an error.

iterator.description: A jq expression selecting the array in the apiRef response to iterate over.

apiVersion.description: Group and version of the referenced resource, for example `widgets.templates.krateo.io/v1beta1`.

verb.description: HTTP verb used to resolve the reference. GET for a read; a mutating verb makes this a write the widget can dispatch.

template.description: The resourcesRefs entry emitted for each iterated element; its fields may interpolate that element.

resourcesRefsTemplate.description: Generates resourcesRefs entries from the apiRef response — one per element the iterator yields — so a widget can reference a list whose length it does not know when authored.

spec.description: The widget's contract: its own data, an optional binding to a RESTAction, the resources it references, and any templated overrides.
